newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ends slightly weaker, but off lows.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ends slightly weaker, but off lows.

text.p: NWE gasoline ended slightly weaker on Tuesday, but had climbed up from earlier levels in afternoon trade on gains in NYMEX gasoline, traders said.
Eurograde barges were done at $188.50 to $190 per tonne fob ARA for April delivery, and were offered at $191.50 in later trade but the seller said bids remained below this level.
Some May Eurograde delivery barrels were later done at $192.
Regular barges were done at $183 in early trade, but bids and offers were stalemated later at $183/$184-85.
Some 0.15 premium material was reported to have traded at $195 per barrel fob ARA.
Traders said supply remained fairly sloppy, but some sellers expressed optimism following gains in NYMEX gasoline.

May gasoline was trading a 0.33 cent higher at 61.05 cents at 1601 GMT, but it was still a far cry from the levels seen this time last year when front-month gasoline futures soared to as high as 68.10 cents.
Players said that while the U.S. arbitrage door remained firmly shut supply would continue to be on the long side.
Swaps were quoted around the $193.75/$194.50 a barrel for May and $2 below that for April.
Traders said the market would be monitoring American Petroleum Institute (API) data out late on Tuesday on the gasoline stock front.
In a Reuters forecast, traders estimated an average fall of 1.5 million barrels in U.S. gasoline stocks in the week ending April 4, against a drop of 335,000 barrels in the week to March 28.

Saudi Aramco was reported to be looking for some 300,000 barrels of 95-octane 0.4 lead content gasoline for early May delivery, but few players thought the material would come out of Europe. --Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
